prompt: Write the command to install the PnP.PowerShell module for the current user only.
hints: Use Install-Module to install modules from the PowerShell Gallery.
The module name is PnP.PowerShell (with a dot, not a hyphen).
Add -Scope CurrentUser to avoid needing admin privileges.

validation.hintOnFail: Add -Scope CurrentUser to install for the current user only.

explanation: Install-Module downloads the PnP.PowerShell module from the PowerShell Gallery. The -Scope CurrentUser flag installs it without requiring administrator privileges.

prompt: Write the command to connect to the SharePoint site https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/IT using interactive browser authentication.
hints: The PnP cmdlet for connecting is Connect-PnPOnline.
Use -Url to specify the SharePoint site URL.

validation.hintOnFail: Include the full SharePoint site URL.

explanation: Connect-PnPOnline establishes a connection to a specific SharePoint site. The -Interactive parameter opens a browser window for you to sign in with your credentials.

prompt: Write the command to connect to Microsoft Graph with scopes for reading all users and reading all groups.
hints: The scope for reading users is User.Read.All.
The scope for reading groups is Group.Read.All.
explanation: Connect-MgGraph authenticates to Microsoft Graph. The -Scopes parameter defines what permissions your session requests. Always request only the permissions you need.

prompt: Write two commands on separate lines: first disconnect from PnP, then disconnect from Microsoft Graph.
hints: Write each command on its own line.

validation.hintOnFail: Include Disconnect-PnPOnline to end the PnP session.
Include Disconnect-MgGraph to end the Graph session.
Disconnect from PnP first, then from Microsoft Graph.

explanation: Always disconnect when finished. Disconnect-PnPOnline clears the PnP session token, and Disconnect-MgGraph clears the Graph session token.
